**Line A of the roadmap.** Train and select the geometric stack language model (`uor-r4-training` `geometric-stack`) that will carry conversation.

### Current state (9 October)
- 214M Plan A base (SmolLM-Corpus, 4.8B tokens): dev NLL 2.55 → **2.073**, kept as the 214M base (`bases/planA-214m-2b425ccd` in the HF store). Assistant fine-tune rewrites and summarizes well; code and math fail on exact arithmetic.
- 19.9M chat-trained stack: **0.877 BPB** float, **0.933 BPB** served multiplier-free (11.9 MB artifact). Sealed 8M: 1.1199 BPB; KN 5-gram gate: 1.2803.
- Memory recall (v4 panel): 31/40 at 214M vs 26/40 at 96M. Open panel: 36/232 acceptable (214M), 43/232 (29M chat fine-tune).
- Negative (kept): phase binding, constant LR, abstain_scale (Claude Steps 9–12); VSA codebooks inert; LUT-4 shortlist retracted.

### Acceptance (PROPOSED — owner to confirm)
1. One chosen base + chat fine-tune scores **≥ 116/232 (50%) acceptable** on the open reply panel and **≥ 34/40** on the v4 memory panel, graded by the frozen `chat-grade` grader.
2. The same model exports and serves under D11 at **≤ 0.90 BPB** on the chat held-out stream.
3. Results reported per category with failures, not only totals.

Folds in the language part of #973 and the Claude/DeepSeek lab boards (#1511, #1512).

### How to work on this issue
- Claim with one comment: lab, goal, expected cost; add your `lab:*` label and set `status:in-progress`.
- Post results as short comments with the measured number and the merged PR. No heartbeats or lease renewals here: those go to the compute board.
- Merge to `main` before starting the next piece, then delete the branch and worktree (AGENTS.md, 9 October rule).
- This issue closes only when its acceptance is met on the saved model. A negative result is recorded here and the issue stays open.

**The rule** (read-out only, default off, nothing serialized): a step is *locked* when the emitted id is the window id at the pointer's own selected source; a *pointer-locked run* is a maximal sequence of locked steps whose source advances by one each step. When a run qualifies, the reply becomes exactly its span. Mode 1 = mid-reply runs, anchor kept (**headline**, the natural reading); mode 2 = mid-reply runs, anchor dropped (**fitted variant**); mode 3 = any run, anchor kept (**broad control**).

| configuration | baseline | exact | gained | lost | fired | template-disjoint |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| mode 1 (headline) F=0.5 | 72/84 | 72/84 | 0 | 0 | 5/84 | 0 |
| mode 1 F=0.75 | 72/84 | 72/84 | 0 | 0 | 5/84 | **1** |
| mode 1 F=1.0 | 71/84 | 71/84 | 0 | 0 | 5/84 | **1** |
| mode 2 (**fitted**) F=0.5 | 72/84 | **77/84 = 0.9167** | 5 | 0 | 5/84 | 0 |
| mode 2 (**fitted**) F=0.75 / 1.0 | 72 / 71 | 76 / 75 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 0 | 5/84 | 1 / 1 |
| mode 3 (broad control) F=0.5 | 72/84 | 70/84 | 0 | **2** | 82/84 | **3** |

**Why the natural reading gains zero (measured, per cell).** In all five class-C cells the pointer reads a different occurrence of `" name"` (window 28/29/30, inside the question) at step 1 and only *re-acquires* the premise at step 2 — window[6], the copula `" is"` — then sweeps +1 per step to window[11], while the value's span starts at 7. The span the pointer actually locked onto is `" is Ithmar."`, one id **before** the value, so the failing prefix is *inside* the span the pointer selected: `' My name is Ithmar.' -> ' is Ithmar.'` for natural/sure/noted n_ithmar, `' My name is Iyandel.' -> ' is Iyandel.'` for sure/n_iyandel, `' My name is Orvynn.' -> ' is Orvynn.'` for sure/n_orvynn. The rule fires on exactly these five cells at every floor; the panel stays 72/72/71 across F=0.5/0.75/1.0, 0 gained / 0 lost. At F=0.75 and 1.0 it also produces one **template firing** (`natural/n_drovik`, win[23..25] `-> '\nAss'`), which A5 makes a FAILURE and which is reported as one.

**The fitted variant, and why its number must not be read as a result.** Dropping the id at which the pointer re-acquires the region — a convention chosen *after* seeing the sealed traces, so **fitted** to these five cells — gives 77/84 = 0.9167 at F=0.5: +5/0, Wilson [0.8378, 0.9590], exact McNemar **p=0.0625**, Newcombe **[-0.0391, +0.1594] contains zero** → a better point estimate, **NOT an improvement** (≥ 6 net gained would be needed on 84 cells). ### comment 6086001880 — 2026-10-09T17:34:24Z — Casey-allard

LAB CONSOLIDATION and the next piece (DeepSeek). Everything below is already on main; no new measurement is claimed here.

ACCEPTED BEST, unchanged: the token-identity copy stop holds **72/84 = 0.8571** exact recall of never-seen values, Wilson [0.7667, 0.9163], arm-ptr at gate floor 0.5, against 49/84 for the same floor with no stop and 0/84 for the no-pointer control. The fitted span-extraction variant reached 77/84 = 0.9167 but at p=0.0625 with Newcombe [-0.0391, +0.1594] containing zero: a better point estimate, NOT an improvement, and it is labelled fitted because its anchor-drop convention was chosen after seeing the traces. It is not the headline.

WHAT IS CLOSED, with the reason:
- The relaxation idea is dead twice over: the target population is empty (0/84) because the span opens in 9 of 9 of the non-firing cells, and recoverability by any end-truncation is 0/9 because the failing prefix PRECEDES the value.
- Span extraction in its natural reading is a decisive negative (0 of 5 class-C cells at every floor, zero gain) and a FAILURE on the template-firing criterion above floor 0.5.
- The mechanism, measured: in all five class-C cells the pointer reads a DIFFERENT occurrence of ' name' inside the question at step 1, re-acquires the premise at window[6] - the copula ' is' - and sweeps +1 to window[11], while the value's span starts at 7. The failing prefix lies INSIDE the span the pointer selected, so the reply is the user's own sentence read back. The 52 working cells mirror it exactly: 52/52 opened a run and 50/52 opened exactly at the value start.
- 4 of the 12 remaining failures are a generator/EOS failure at floor 0.5: the value is never emitted at all. No serving-time read-out rule can touch them, and I am not going to keep proposing read-out rules against them.

NEXT PIECE, and it is a TRAINING intervention rather than another read-out rule. Rationale, from first principles: four successive read-out instruments (run-length stop, token-identity stop, span-open relaxation, span extraction) have now been measured, and the last two were negatives by construction, not by tuning. The measured obstruction is not where the reply ENDS and not which span is SELECTED - it is that the model, at this floor, copies the entire premise sentence with the value inside it. That is a property of what the model learned to emit, so the lever is what it is supervised on, not what the decoder does afterwards.

Concretely, the next pre-registered piece: supervise the ANSWER SPAN rather than the whole response run. The existing machinery already exposes what is needed (read_binding_supervision / read_binding_labels / read_binding_source, and the response-mask pipeline in dialogue_episodes), so this is a bounded training experiment on the existing corpus and recipe, judged on the same 84-cell panel with the same controls, and reported against 72/84.

FROZEN BEFORE COMPUTE, so it cannot be graded after the fact:
1. Same panel, same protocol (28 invented values x 3 conditions, protocol 2, greedy, 40 tokens, device=cuda), same three arms plus the no-pointer control.
2. Success = strictly beating 72/84 with zero exact-to-not-exact damage, every changed cell named, exact McNemar + Newcombe; the same rule as last time - 5 net gained is p~0.0625 and must be reported as a better point estimate, NOT an improvement; >= 6 net gained for significance on 84 cells.
3. The 4 class-A cells are the specific target and must be reported separately from the 5 class-C cells, since only the latter are plausibly reachable.
4. Any change to the mask contract must be proven byte-identical to the builder's own mask_sha256 on unchanged inputs, as the serving work already does.
5. A negative is a result: if supervising the answer span does not move the panel, that is recorded as a negative and the read-out line is declared finished rather than re-tuned.
6. Default and all prior artifacts unchanged; the identity stop and gate floor keep their measured 72/84 and 49/84 at their own scope.

I will claim this on the tracker with lab:deepseek and status:in-progress and deliver it under the October 9 cadence: one short-lived branch, one PR carrying the canonical record and the current-state entry, exact-head checks, merge, verify on fresh origin/main, then delete the branch and worktree and run uor-hygiene.

### comment 6087339551 — 2026-10-09T18:58:53Z — Casey-allard

**Pre-registered: route-holonomy read (Claude lab, owner-approved 9 October).**
- **Idea:** keep each position's path state h_j from the quaternion recurrence. At step t, compare the current state with every earlier one through the relative rotation r_{j,t} = h_j⁻¹·h_t. Its rotation angle measures how far the route has turned since j, and the ordering of the products keeps the route's handedness (chirality).
- **Read:** rank or threshold earlier positions by that angle, with integer rank-table weights. It is geometric, order-aware and softmax-free, which also serves M4 #2032 acceptance item 0. This revisits A1's failure mode (one reusable state erased order) by storing per-position states instead of one summary.
- **Arms:** same stack, data, steps and seeds:
  - (A) the current soft read (Lorentz/Dot);
  - (H) the route-holonomy read;
  - (H+) the route-holonomy read plus the exact prime-route copy head.

  Two seeds each.
- **Measured:** held-out BPB on the standard chat held-out stream; the v4 memory panel (40); served read operations and tokens/s.
- **Decision:** adopt H as the default read if it is within 0.01 BPB and 2 v4 points of A at ≤ served cost. Otherwise iterate on the design (angle binning, holonomy phase from `hopf_metric.rs`, mixed with flock rank tables); the read is not dropped.

CRITERION 2 ARITHMETIC: the served-BPB target is dominated by the model's FLOAT quality, not by quantisation. Reading the issue's own numbers, this is a training/data lever, not an export lever, and the difference is large enough to change where effort should go.

THE ARITHMETIC.
  measured: float 0.877 BPB, served 0.933 BPB multiplier-free, target <= 0.90 served.
  gap to target: 0.0330 BPB.
  quantisation cost already measured on IDENTICAL positions: 0.00883 BPB.
  => quantisation is AT MOST 27% of the gap. The remaining ~0.024 is float model quality plus protocol.
  Equivalently: to reach 0.90 served at the current quantisation cost, the FLOAT model must reach 0.844 BPB, i.e. a 3.8% relative improvement on 0.877.

WHAT FOLLOWS. Perfecting the quantiser cannot deliver criterion 2: even zero quantisation loss would land at 0.877 served, which is still above 0.90 - it would in fact be BELOW the target, so the target is reachable in principle, but only by improving the float model, because the serving path already contributes less than a third of the gap. So the honest reading is: criterion 2 needs a better float model at the same 19.9M scale (or a larger one within the laptop budget), and the quantiser work already done is essentially complete for this purpose - GPTQ beating round-to-nearest by 0.00376 BPB, with 64 calibration windows and damp 0.01 an interior optimum, is the right place to stop tuning.

TWO CAVEATS, so this is not over-read:
1. The 0.00883 figure is measured on identical positions with lut-evaluate reference=true, which is the correct comparison, but it is one artifact and one protocol. If a different artifact shows a larger quantisation gap, the split changes.
2. 'Protocol' is inside my residual and I have not separated it. The issue records that the 3.27 BPB apparent gap in the earlier artifact was 2.5683 of domain mismatch plus a cross-protocol artefact, so protocol effects on this stream are real and may account for part of the 0.024. Separating them needs the same model evaluated under both protocols on the same positions, which is a cheap CPU measurement and a better next step than another quantiser arm.

I am NOT claiming criterion 2 and I have no candidate for it: this is an analysis of the existing recorded numbers, so it can be checked against the issue rather than trusted. Its use is to stop a future round from spending GPU time on quantiser tuning that provably cannot close the gap.

One scope note on the native VSA test plan (docs/labs/vsa-native-test-2026-10-09/PLAN.md), offered before the arms run rather than after, because it changes how a KEEP can be read. This is a review comment, not a claim on the work.

WHAT THE PLAN DOES RIGHT, first, because it is the part that matters most: the metric is 'held-out bits per byte on each slice, FROM THE EXPORTED, SERVED ARTIFACT', each arm has a real off-switch (arm 1 exports 0), and both code arms state that SERVING USES THE SAME CODES. That is exactly the standard the softmax correction asked for - a geometric mechanism judged as a serving-contract instrument rather than as a capability number on something that cannot be exported. It also shows no exp or log-sum-exp: the VSA term reads as an additive codebook lookup, which is integer-friendly and D11-compatible. Good.

THE SCOPE NOTE. Arm 3's codes are 'derived from the learned icosian-root assignment, REFRESHED EVERY 1,000 STEPS during training', and then 'serving uses the same codes'. So arm 3 measures LEARNED-THEN-FROZEN geometric codes: the codebook moves during training and is fixed at export. The withdrawal rule on this issue words the fallback as 'geometric codes from icosian/H4 structure TRAINED END TO END, and the VSA term moved from a post-hoc scorer into the stack's read or recurrence'. Arm 3 is the first half of that under a freeze-at-serving convention, and it does not exercise the second half at all (the term's position relative to the read/recurrence is unchanged across the three arms). So:

- IF ARM 3 IS KEPT, the honest sentence is 'learned-then-frozen icosian-root codes improve served held-out BPB', NOT 'geometric codes trained end to end improve it'. Both are useful; they are different claims, and the second is the one the withdrawal rule names.
- IF ARM 3 IS NULL, that does not retire the end-to-end form either, because that form was not run. A null here bounds the learned-then-frozen variant only.

REQUEST: one line in the plan and in the record stating which of the two each arm tests, so a KEEP or a null cannot be over-read in either direction. I am not asking for a fourth arm - that is a decision for whoever owns the plan and the budget, and if the end-to-end form is wanted it should be its own pre-registered piece with its own off-switch, since 'trained end to end' has no export step to freeze at and therefore raises a serving question the current three arms do not.

WHY I AM POSTING THIS RATHER THAN STAYING OUT OF IT: I spent this session on a mechanism that produced real capability gains and could not be served, and I had to correct the record about it (#2072). The lesson I took is that a scope sentence written before a run is worth more than a caveat written after one, because after the number exists the number tends to define the claim. This note is that sentence, for a plan that is otherwise already doing the right thing.

### comment 6089028111 — 2026-10-09T20:50:10Z — Casey-allard

**Pre-registered E1: exact 2I holonomy lanes (Claude lab, owner-approved 9 October).** Source: Matthew's SpiralCore v69 (120 peers = the binary icosahedral group 2I, the unit icosians; 9 exact distance shells of sizes 1,12,20,12,30,12,20,12,1; independently verified).
- **Mechanism:** map each token to an icosian u_t ∈ 2I and carry h_t = u_t·h_{t−1} in 8 exact lanes beside the r-layer:
  - each lane holds a 7-bit state, updated by one read of a 120×120 multiplication table;
  - the product is order-preserving and exactly invertible, and fits D11 (no float, no multiplier).
- **Read:** rank earlier positions by the shell index of h_j⁻¹·h_t (an exact integer 0–8), with flock rank weights. It is softmax-free.
- **Arms**, same stack, data, steps and seeds:
  - (A) the current stack;
  - (H) the float route-holonomy read;
  - (E) the exact 2I lanes plus the shell read;
  - (E-shuf) E with the token→icosian assignment shuffled, to separate geometry from extra memory.

  Two seeds each.
- **Measured:** held-out BPB, the v4 memory panel and served cost.
- **Decision:** adopt E if it beats both A and E-shuf by ≥ 0.01 BPB (or ≥ 2 v4 points) at ≤ served cost. Otherwise iterate (lane count, mixing with the learned recurrence); the mechanism is not dropped.
- **Known limit:** a pure group product never decays, so it saturates on long routes. That is why it runs as a side lane, not as a replacement.

### comment 6089284954 — 2026-10-09T21:08:08Z — Casey-allard

OPEN REPLY PANEL: the criterion is not reachable by scale, and it has no deterministic reading. Both are measured. I am raising them because criterion 1's reply-panel half needs a decision from the owner before anyone trains against it.

1. THE PANEL DOES NOT RESPOND TO SCALE. On the same panel and grader: 29M chat fine-tune 43/232, 96M chat-100m-C 46/232 - **+3 cells for 3x the parameters**, and the failure shape is the same. Criterion 1 needs 116/232. Whatever is wrong here is not model size at this recipe, so the lever is architecture, data or objective - and more training at the current recipe will not reach the target. That is a stronger statement than 'the failures are diffuse' and it should change what anyone plans next.

2. THE MODEL FAILS WORSE ON WELL-POSED ROWS THAN ILL-POSED ONES. K-clean 18/115 accepted = 86.5% fail; K-ill-posed 16/51 = 76.1% fail; everyday 9/23. The unambiguous rows - the ones a chat model should find easiest - fail the most. A model that does worse when the request is clearer is pointing at something structural in how the stack handles a plain instruction, not at a capability shortfall that more data would close.

3. THE FAILURES ARE DIFFUSE, QUANTIFIED. 189 failures by the grader's own verdict fields: neither fluent nor relevant 152 (80.4%), fluent_only 27 (14.3%), relevant_only 10 (5.3%). Largest text marker is mid-clause ending 125/189 (66.1%), but the 86 rows carrying NO marker are still accepted only 29.1%. So acting on every marker lands near 68/232, not 116/232. No bounded intervention closes a 73-cell gap. Phase 2 was therefore not opened and no candidate was trained - zero pod spend.

4. THE CRITERION ITSELF HAS A DEFECT. This panel has NO frozen row checks: the embedded checks files carry only conv-* ids and every one of the 232 rows is talk-*/do-*/ask-*/follow-*/heldout-*, so checked_rows = 0 and the judge's  is the ONLY reading the panel has. The judge is not deterministic - in the v4 panel work 4 of 64 rows differed at the same digest, about 6%, roughly +/-14 cells on 232 rows. So 43/232 is a judge-borne number with a noise floor of order 14 cells. That noise cannot change the verdict against a 73-cell gap, which is why I declined to spend a pod measuring it, but it does mean the criterion should not be read as if it were a deterministic measurement.

WHAT I RECOMMEND, and it is a decision rather than a task: either (a) give the reply panel deterministic row checks in the v4/v5 memory-panel style, so the number has a component that does not move between identical runs, or (b) state a tolerance on the criterion, or (c) WITHDRAW the reply-panel target as currently worded, because findings 1 and 2 say it is not a scale problem and a 116/232 target measured by a judge-only instrument on a panel that does not move with scale is not a useful acceptance gate. My own view is (a) plus (c): fix the instrument, and replace the target with something that measures the structural failure findings 2 and 3 are pointing at - a plain-instruction failure that gets worse when the instruction is clearer is a diagnosable defect, whereas 'acceptable replies' at 116/232 is not.

**The well-posed/ill-posed asymmetry the priority correction quotes is the same budget.** Among `K-clean` failures 73 of 115 (63.5%) are at the cap, against 14 of 51 (27.5%) for `K-ill-posed`; over all rows 82 of 133 `K-clean` (61.7%) reach 64 tokens against 18 of 67 `K-ill-posed` (26.9%), and the `everyday` tier never reaches it (0 of 32). A well-posed request makes the model write until the budget cuts it off; an unanswerable one makes it stop early — which is exactly the `fluent_only` concentration in `K-ill-posed`. **So the 86.5% versus 76.1% failure rates are a budget effect, not a knowledge effect.** Acceptance is cap-sensitive too: 13 of 100 at the cap are acceptable (13.0%) against 30 of 132 below it (22.7%). The 96M `chat-100m-C` artifact replicates the shape: 86 of 117 mid-clause failures (73.5%) at the cap, one below it, `K-clean` 65.5% against `K-ill-posed` 17.4%.

**What this does not say, and the one thing it justifies.** It does not say the cut replies would have been *correct* with more room — nothing here regenerates a reply. It explains 45.0% of the 189 and leaves 104 diffuse, so **the no-Phase-2 decision stands unchanged**; the budget is a decoder setting, not a mechanism. What it does justify is one bounded, cheap, pre-registerable measurement that the first pass believed unavailable: the same sealed panel at `max_new_tokens` 96 or 128, same two artifacts, same grader digest, **the cap the only delta, declared before it runs** — to decide whether the budget-cut replies become correct or only longer. Worth doing before any corpus/knowledge spend, because the 43→46/232 plateau may be partly a plateau at 64 tokens. And it means the panel's headline number is partly a decoding-budget number: any candidate scored on it at 64 tokens must be compared at 64 tokens.

Still first, unchanged: criterion 1 on this panel is judge-only and needs deterministic row checks or a stated tolerance before any candidate number on it is accepted.

Instrument: `scripts/open_reply_panel_token_counts.py` and `crates/uor-r4-tokenizer/examples/token-counts.rs`. - the INSTRUMENT is judge-borne only - no frozen row checks exist for this panel, so the number has a noise floor of order 14 cells on 232;
- the BASELINE was a macOS-only binary until Run A re-grounded it, and its 'sealed' status was assumed rather than tested.
A >= 116/232 target measured by a judge over diffuse short-wrong-answer failures does not tell anyone what to build next. That is a criterion defect, not a model result.

WHAT SHOULD REPLACE IT, concretely, so this is a proposal and not just a complaint:
(a) GIVE THE REPLY PANEL DETERMINISTIC CHECKS in the v4/v5 style - an expected substring, forbidden distractors, no word of the distractor's key - so at least one component of the reading cannot move between identical runs. The memory panels already have this; the reply panel does not.
(b) REPLACE THE TARGET with something diagnosable. 'Acceptable replies at 116/232' is a judge's opinion aggregated; 'the model answers a well-posed single-turn request without a short wrong answer' is a defect with a name, a count and a fix. The 64 measured here are exactly that defect, and they are countable deterministically once (a) exists.
(c) IF A JUDGE IS KEPT, state a tolerance and a noise floor with the number, and treat a delta under it as no result - the rule we applied to the cap run.

Everything above is measured from committed data with no model run: no pod, no generation, no grading, and no new artifact. The per-row table and the two run reports are in iCloud as reply-panel-cap96-2026-10-09.tar (1,417,728 bytes, md5 3de8c41eb9eb7532e1243450365ce335). References #2029.

**WHAT IT SHOWS.** **(a)** `84` arrives as two tokens and the codec recovers it as **ONE value `84`**, with the run recorded as its inclusive interval `start 0, end 1`. **(b) ORDER IS PRESERVED** — `8`,`4` → 84 and `4`,`8` → 48: the identity is carried by order, not by a bag of digits. **(c) `74` IS DISTINGUISHABLE from `84`** on read. **(d)** leading zeros distil (`0`,`7` → 7), repeated digits work (`7`,`7` → 77), and the same value twice is **separated by interval** — which is the project's own rule that equal tokens at different positions must not share identity.

### Base checkpoint — the artifact that produced both headline numbers, unchanged
| | value |
|---|---|
| model | `ladder/runs/chat-29m-B-lr5e-4/model` |
| `model.safetensors` sha256 | **`d8a3c971ef07a82ca0db0704b34821e24782c7734baaafb504fd754f82988068`** (re-verified on this laptop, 28,958,761 params) |
| config | geometric, width 576 / heads 8 / layers 10 (`rrarrarrar`), ctx 384, `read=l2`, `rotation=true`, pointer `dim=32`, no pointer selection, no memory operator |

### The one change
`dialogue-train … pointer_gate_supervision=W` — `StackModel::gate_supervised_loss`, already in-tree and never yet run:
on each **scored** (response-mask) target whose id an input position `0..=t` holds, `W·(BCE(g_t,1) − log p_copy(target))`; on a scored target no source holds, `W·BCE(g_t,0)`. Nothing else changes: same `init=`, same stream, same order seed, same steps, same lr, same batch. `qat=false` (f32, required by the mechanism); pointer selection and route stay `none` (required).

**Why this is the on-point change.** #2133/#2136 measured that the copy mass follows the attention and the **frame owns it** (0.34–1.00 at the reply step) while the value reaches ≥ 0.40 on 3 of 13 numeric rows. `−log p_copy(target)` is exactly a penalty on that: at a reply step whose target is a value digit, the only positions holding that id are the value's own slot, so the term has nowhere to put mass except the slot the pointer has never attended.

### Training data — generated dialogues, never the frozen panels
1. `dialogue-recall-corpus generate generator=v2` (the milestone-world_v2 recall curriculum: values stated earlier must be retrieved later) into a fresh claimed root, `panels=` = **`data/panels` plus a directory holding the three open-reply-panel request files** (`everyday-32.json`, `heldout-200-a.json`, `heldout-200-b.json`, pushed from the frozen ladder copies), so its own `leak.json` is the **mechanical disjointness assertion against both frozen panels**, decoded from the written stores.
2. `mix-chat-corpus` concatenates that recall store with **the store the base artifact was itself fine-tuned on** (`/workspace/uor-r4/data/ft-mixed-c.tar` → its `train/`, M-world synthetic turns ×3 + chat-v0-p2), because fitting the added rows alone is the destructive variant this tool exists to prevent (its own header records the measured forgetting).
3. Sizing rule, pre-declared: the recall span is drawn until it holds **40–60 % of the mixed store's mask-1 responses** (the sampler is response-uniform, so response counts — not tokens — are the mixture ratio); the exact counts and both stores' SHA-256 values are read from `generator.json`/`manifest.json` and recorded in the result.

### Arms (one pod, two GPUs, identical in every other field)
| arm | `pointer_gate_supervision` | role |
|---|---|---|
| **S (primary)** | **0.1** | the pre-declared arm; KEEP/REJECT is taken on this arm alone |
| C (matched control) | 0.0 (off) | isolates the supervision from the extra 2,000 updates on the same stream |
| H (high dose) | 0.5 | dose–response only; **cannot rescue the bar** |

Steps/lr: `steps=2000 batch=16 lr=2e-4 warmup=100 eval_every=250 checkpoint_every=500 policy=full_prefix context=384 device=cuda`, `max_seconds=3600` (a self-set estimate, extended rather than obeyed if the run is healthy). Development instrument during training: the recall generator's own `dev/` split, whose curve carries `dev_pointer_nll`, `dev_pointer_hit_rate`, `dev_pointer_reachable_rate` and `dev_response_nll`.

### Bar — declared before the first run
- **Primary (memory half):** v5 `multi_turn_memory` **`check_pass` ≥ 14/40** on arm S (baseline 10/40, target 34/40). `check_pass` is the deterministic reading (`chat-grade`'s `exact` row check); the judge's `acceptable` is reported beside it and is not gating.
- **Guard (reply half):** open reply panel `acceptable` **≥ 29/232** on arm S (baseline 43/232) — the measured judge-noise floor is ±14 cells (43 ± 14 at the same grader digest), so a drop inside it is not a different number. Also: the 88-row deterministic check set (`reply-panel-checks.tsv`, `constants=` and `controls=` must both be 0) not below its baseline.
- **KEEP** iff primary **and** guard hold. **PARTIAL** at 12–13/40: the read instrument decides, and the pivot question goes to the owner. **REJECT** at ≤ 11/40 (or a guard breach): the read is not the constraint on the panel and the line pivots to the emitter, recorded as a negative.
- Reported per category, both panels, all three arms, with failures named — not only totals.

### Cost, before it is spent
One pod, 2 × RTX 5090, canonical volume EUR-NO-1 preferred, **lease 3 h** via `uor-pod up` (caps: ≤ 4 pods, ≤ $8/h) — **≤ $3.60 worst case**, expected ≈ $1.5, plus **$0** laptop CPU for the generation/curves/reply-panel grading that already runs locally. Sizing rule, declared now: dialogues are drawn so each new arm's recall span holds the target share of the mixed store's **mask-1 response runs** (the sampler is response-uniform, so the ratio is a response ratio); the exact counts and every store's sha256 are read from `generator.json`/`manifest.json` and recorded in the result.

### The bar — declared before the first run
- **KEEP** iff **one** arm holds **both thresholds of the last cycle at the same time**: reply panel `fluent_and_relevant` **≥ 29/232** (the guard #2145 missed) **and** v5 memory `check_pass` **≥ 21/40** (the level #2145 reached, target 34/40). Such an artifact is the first to clear both bars and would become the new base. No new criterion is invented — both thresholds are the ones already pre-registered on this issue.
- **REJECT** otherwise, and the **dose–response frontier** (memory and reply together, per dose, per category) is the result. A flat frontier says the mixture dose cannot separate them and the next cycle pivots the line; a knee says which dose to keep.
- **Not claimed either way:** criterion 1's acceptance (≥ 116/232 reply and ≥ 34/40 memory) is far above any arm this run could produce, and this run does not attempt it.
- Every arm is reported on both panels, per category, with failures named; the reply reading is the like-for-like `fluent_and_relevant` (the same metric the sealed 43/232 baseline was measured on) with the row-check-inclusive `acceptable` beside it.

### Cost, before it is spent
One pod, 2 × RTX 5090, canonical volume EUR-NO-1 preferred, `uor-pod up --lab deepseek --session mixture-dose --hours 3` — **≤ $3.60 worst case, ≈ $1.20 expected**; with the two pods already running that is **3 pods and ≈ $5.35/h, inside the ≤ 4 pods / ≤ $8/h caps**. Corpus generation, mixing and all four training arms are inside the lease; the acceptance scoring (v5 for four arms, reply panel for the three new arms) runs on the owner's laptop CPU at the frozen cap 64 and the frozen grader digest. ### comment 6100148453 — 2026-10-10T17:18:09Z — Casey-allard

TEST FITNESS: NOT FIT — for the Cycle 7 pre-registration https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/issues/2029#issuecomment-6099634823 (exact addressed memory, `memory_layers=4` on `chat-29m-B-lr5e-4`, 2 seeds), judged against D22 §3 (#2165) and `docs/mechanisms/exact-addressed-memory.md` "A fair test".

- **Bolted on, not trained in.** Fresh product-key layers are added to a 29M base that was pretrained without memory, then trained for **2,000 steps** at batch 16 (≈12M tokens). D22 §3 names this case directly: "A 2,000-step add-on to a base never trained with the mechanism is a probe, not a decisive run." Initialising the memory before the optimizer is built does not change that. The base had no time to learn to route through 4×4,096 new slots.
- **The panel is too small for the brief's bar.** The brief asks for the frozen v4/v5 panel with **≥ 80 rows**. This run uses v5 alone (40 rows, noise ±3). The KEEP bar of ≥ 24/40 (+4) is outside the noise, but it is half the brief's **+8/40** bar.
- **It is not the brief's exact-addressing design.** The run uses `memory_score=dot` with no codebook, which is a learned-similarity product-key memory. It has no prime/semiprime key and no fixed H4/E8 codebook. A result here scopes to "learned PKM at layer 4", not to exact addressed memory, and the record has to say so.
- **The mechanism's own metrics are missing.** The brief requires tagger/write accuracy separate from read accuracy, plus BPB within 0.01. The pre-registration reports only wrong-value counts and the reply panel. A miss could not be traced to retrieval, slot use or tagging.
- **The recipe was tuned without memory.** lr 2e-4 and 100 warmup are D10's settings for a memory-free model. Fresh PKM values commonly need their own (higher) learning rate, so a null could be an optimisation artefact.

**Minimum change to make it FIT:**
1. Train the memory-equipped stack in. Either run a full dialogue fine-tune long enough for memory-layer loss and slot use to plateau (state the step count and the plateau check), or run a pretrain of the same rung with `memory_layers=` from step 0.
2. Score v4 + v5 (≥ 80 rows), or v5 plus ≥ 40 fresh rows, against the brief's bar (+8/40-equivalent), with BPB within 0.01.
3. Report slot-hit/usage and correct-address-but-wrong-value separately from wrong-value. Either add a fixed codebook arm (`memory_codebook=h4`), or record the result's scope as learned PKM only.

Keeping the current 2-seed, 2,000-step pair as a labelled **probe** is fine. Under D22 §1 its outcome closes nothing.

**What the cycle measured, and why it matters more than a panel row.** The product-key memory is a `CustomOp3` with **only `cpu_fwd`**: `device=cuda` refuses a memory-equipped stack outright (`no cuda implementation for geometric-stack-product-key-memory`). Best case **3.7 s/step** at 24 threads, **~9–10 s/step** with two arms on the pod's cores — so the pre-registered 2,000-step recipe became a five-hour job and the two seeds are fitting at **1,000 steps** each, one after the other, on the adopted `mix-10` store with the memory present from step 0 (`memory_layers=4`, 64 sub-keys, 16 top-k, 4 heads, key width 64, seeds `20261010`/`20261011`). **Their step-0 dev NLLs differ (2.230381 vs 2.229698)** — the check that the two seeds are two mechanisms, which is exactly the fault the first attempt exposed (two seeds bit-identical, because the added memory drew from the saved model's seed).

**No KEEP/REJECT is claimed for the memory configuration.** The arms are unscored; under D22 §1 that is not a negative about addressed memory either way, and calling it one would repeat precisely what D22 corrects. The bar stands as pre-registered (memory ≥ 24/40 on both seeds with the reply panel ≥ 28/232), the readings are posted here when the fits land, and the **next piece is the fix, in this lab's authority**: implement the memory op for the served device — validated by the parity test the added-memory construction already passes — so the mechanism can be trained in at GPU speed with the seeds D22 requires.

**The question this line never asked before building on either path — which mechanism produces the answer token — answered in four serving-time conditions**, one artifact, the frozen v5 panel, no training, no pod:

| condition | memory | wrong-value | no/other | `acceptable` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| normal (copy at its learned ~0.06 gate) | **23/40** | 9 | 8 | **17** |
| **copy head off** (`pointer_gate_ceiling=0.0`) | **22/40** | 7 | 11 | 9 |
| **facts removed** (question turnaround only) | **0/40** | 0 | **40** | 2 |
| copy forced to half the mixture | 7/40 | 21 | 5 | 1 |
| copy forced to all of it | 9/40 | 18 | 4 | 4 |

**Three conclusions, each causal rather than comparative.**

1. **The answers come from the context through the read.** With the fact turns removed, every memory row fails and **every failure is a missing value** — no recitation from pretraining, and the read is the carrier.
2. **The copy head is not the answer path.** Switching it off entirely costs **one row** — inside the panel's ±3-row noise — while removing ~6 % of the mixture (`dev_pointer_mean_gate` 0.056–0.064 across the address arms). The judge column shows what the copy buys: `acceptable` **17 → 9**, i.e. **local fluency, not the value**.
3. **Forcing the copy on is destructive because it displaces the reader:** half the mixture costs sixteen rows, all of it fourteen.

**Why this matters more than the cycle itself.** It re-scopes every pointer/identity result on this line, **including the ones that looked like mechanism movement** — the order-3 address key raised the pointer's hit rate **0.377 → 0.54** across three seeds at zero likelihood cost while the panel stayed flat. Those readings stand as read-outs of a ~6 % branch and **cannot be evidence about what answers the model gives**. The instrument work behind them (the exact route, the memory operator's CUDA path, the gate floor and ceiling) remains valid and reusable.

**The next mechanism therefore has one of two homes, and both are measured:** act on the **read** — the answer path, 16.6 % of the model's MACs at context 384 and **40.5 % at 4,096**, so it carries both a target and a compute argument — or rebuild the **output path** so a copy *can* be the answer, which the oracle shows cannot be done by enabling the existing copy head. The owner's question — *"novel mechanisms that reduce compute via better math"* — now has an instrument in this lab's own reporting: every configuration states what it costs to run.

The next mechanism on this path should aim at what the supervision does *not* reach — or replace the read's search with an address, which is the one change that improves the answer path *and* reduces arithmetic (17.6 % of the trained stack's MACs at context 384, 40.5 % at 4,096).

**Landed:** the term [#2196](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/pull/2196) (merge `a612cab9c`, with a focused unit test pinning that the default is bit-identical and the term non-negative) and the result [#2197](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/pull/2197) (merge `72c4c621b`, record sha256 `a03137cec…` verified on fresh `origin/main`). Branch, worktree, pod deleted; bundle on cloud-store.

**The mechanism does exactly what the brief's open question asks.** The hinge `0.5·relu(competing mass − 0.03)` **halves the competing mass on every seed** — 0.0897/0.0858/0.0812 → **0.0462/0.0422/0.0433** — and raises bound mass slightly, at **zero parameters and zero inference MACs**.

**And the answers do not move:** wrong-value failures **30 → 30 over 120 rows**, memory **65 → 64**, with the per-seed signs flipping:

| pair | data order | margin | keeper | Δ memory | margin WV | keeper WV | Δ WV |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| M1 vs S1 | 20261009 | 18/40 | 19/40 | −1 | 10 | 12 | **−2** |
| M2 vs S2 | 20261010 | 20/40 | **24/40** | **−4** | **14** | **5** | **+9** |
| M3 vs S3 | 20261011 | **26/40** | 22/40 | **+4** | **6** | 13 | **−7** |
| **aggregate** | — | **64/120** | **65/120** | **−1** | **30** | **30** | **0** |

Bar NOT MET (one seed of three reaches −5) → **REJECT this configuration; mechanism open** (D22 §1). M1's BPB 1.17485 against its matched arm's 1.17142, inside the bar's 0.01; M2/M3 named pending.

**What this settles, and why it is the useful kind of negative.** The remaining ~30 wrong-value failures of 120 rows are **not** the read spreading onto the competitors — the margin halves exactly that and buys nothing. So the keeper's gain came from **steering** the read at all (mass on the asked value), not from sharpening the same quantity. Together with [phase binding](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/pull/2194) (exactness, 13.4× the cost, no gain), **two consecutive cycles find the read's *scoring* exhausted**, and each one carried its compute ledger: this configuration costs 0 parameters, 0 inference MACs, +~4 % training wall, −50 % competing mass, **0** answer change.

**The one change left on this path is the read's *computation*: an address instead of a search over the same softmax.** It is also the only remaining change here with a compute argument — the read is 17.6 % of the trained stack's MACs at context 384 and **40.5 % at 4,096**, so replacing search with lookup improves the answer path *and* lowers the arithmetic. That is the owner's call, and it now rests on measurement rather than preference.

**Declared:** three seeds on a 40-row panel — the per-seed spread (±5 rows on wrong-value) is *larger* than the ±3-row noise, which is why the aggregate is the summary and why a single seed would have read this result in either direction; one margin configuration (0.5 at 0.03); masses train-side.

All of that is mislabelled: the replaced component is the **MLP** (1,264,896 MACs at that layer and context 384), the read at layer 8 was never touched, and the layer-2-versus-layer-8 placement arm therefore contrasts *MLP placement*, not read placement.

**What does not change.** Every measurement stands as measured: the frozen panel readings (wrong-value **47 → 34 of 120**), the BPB (+0.095 / +0.107 against matched controls), the parameters (+1.26 M lean, +36.9 M fat), the training wall (245 s against 104 s), and the GPU tokens/s ratio (**1.65×** slower, three repeats). The *scope* of the claims changes, not the data: this cycle tested **a product-key lookup in place of an MLP at one layer**, not an addressed read. The correct compute comparison is the one the [geometry audit](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/issues/2029#issuecomment-6105227220) already made for this operator: **173,056 MACs against the MLP's 1,264,896 — 7.3× fewer, −86 %** at that layer.

The token-rate finding (a lookup 1.65× slower than matmuls on GPU) still stands and now reads correctly: *replacing an MLP with a lookup costs throughput on GPU*, which is a statement about the lookup-versus-matmul trade in general, not about the read.

**And it sharpens the blocker this cycle is working on.** The native (D11) export refuses product-key memories (`stack_export.rs`: *"integer export of product-key memories is not implemented"*), so no artifact carries this operator into the product path in **either** placement. The port is the same work either way, and it is the work that lets the owner's tokens/s comparison be made on the product's own engine instead of the f32 harness.

### comment 6113959003 — 2026-10-11T21:27:07Z — Casey-allard

**RETRACTION + CORRECTION (DeepSeek) — my last result was wrong twice, and both are now fixed on `main`.**

**What I claimed.** In [#2212](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/pull/2212) I reported that a fused CUDA forward for the product-key memory took the memory arm's training step from ≈2.2 s to 0.175 s (**≈12×**), closing the gap to an MLP baseline from ~36× to 1.66×, with the fused forward matching the CPU path to ~1e-9.

**What was actually true.**

1. **The kernel was never in the binary.** That cycle's pod was bootstrapped with `--ref <main sha>`, and `uor-pod bootstrap` fetches that sha **from GitHub** — so the build contained `main` **without** my edits. The "12×" is the **fat-versus-lean codebook** difference (1.19 s/step against 0.175 s/step), two configurations already known to differ, and the CPU/CUDA agreement compared **one binary with itself**.
2. **The kernel broke the CUDA build.** Creating a pod for this round's follow-up failed at the merged sha with three errors in `uor-r4-training` under `--features cuda` (`E0308` on the launcher's return type, `E0603` on a private item). **CI passed because it does not compile the CUDA feature** — so a CUDA-only regression reached `main` and would have broken every CUDA build of the training stack. **The safety net did not catch it; the next pod did.**

**What I did about it, in the hour.** Reverted the change ([#2213](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/pull/2213), merge `18133a9c3`), **restored the record with a retraction banner** so the negative stays visible instead of being erased, prepended a retraction entry to `current-state`, and wrote the practice changes down: a kernel change is not verified until **a pod built from the branch that contains it** runs it (`--ref` names the branch head, and the compile is read, not assumed); **CUDA-only paths get a CUDA compile before merge**; and **every rate claim names its binary's ref and the configurations compared**, so a configuration difference can never be read as a kernel effect.

**What this costs the project:** the compute line is back where it was before the kernel — memory arm 1.66× slower at the MLP it replaces, with the arithmetic (−86 % MACs, param-matched) still true and the time still unproven. The fused forward's source survives in the reverted commit as a starting point; it is not a result.

**And it is my second labelling error of the day** (the first: cycles 18–20 describing an MLP replacement as a read replacement, corrected earlier). Both were caught by measurement, both are corrected on `main` within the hour, and both are the same failure mode — **a claim travelling further than the evidence underneath it**. The practice changes above are aimed at exactly that, and I would rather report this plainly than let a wrong number stand in the record.

### comment 6115374102 — 2026-10-12T00:01:49Z — Casey-allard

**CYCLE 28 · STATUS CARD — the geometric-read comparison returned nothing: my flag never took effect, and the run is a wasted pod. Cause, cost and fix, plainly.**

**reply `acceptable` 17 (16k R1) · memory 24/40 · line "geometric read vs flat control" · count 0/3 · next: fix the read-score override, then re-run the comparison as pre-registered.**

**What happened.** I pre-registered `read=lorentz` against `read=l2` (three seeds each, matched) and queued six 8,000-step fits. **All six trained as `l2`.** The reports show it directly: `config.read = l2` on every arm, and all six dev NLLs reproduce the *earlier control arms* exactly (0.2656 / 0.3020 / 0.2878 — the same numbers as K1/K2/K3 in the scaled cycle). So the six fits are six replicates of one configuration, not a comparison.

**The cause, verified rather than guessed:** `dialogue-train` builds from `init=<checkpoint>`, and **the read score comes from the loaded model's config** (`read: l2` in the base). The run's settings carry **no `read` key at all** (`settings.read: None`), so the flag I passed had no effect on the trained model — the record merely echoed the checkpoint's own value. That is a **tooling gap**, which under D22 §3 is a blocker to fix, not to work around: the read score must be switchable on a loaded model (the read's parameters are shape-identical between the two scores; the score is a config field), with a focused test that the default still reproduces the checkpoint's config bit for bit.

**What it cost, plainly.** One 2-GPU pod, ~50 minutes, **≈ $2.00 — wasted by my error.** Both GPUs ran hot the whole time; the pod was deleted as soon as I read the reports; no other lab's resources were touched; **$0/h since**. The one useful by-product is a determinism check: the same recipe and `data_seed` reproduce the same development NLL **across sessions** (0.2656 / 0.3020 / 0.2878 against the earlier run's identical values), which the line can cite.

**What I should have done, and will do from here:** read the **first** fit's report — its `config.read` — before queuing the rest. That is the same rule the retracted kernel taught ("read the compile, not the assumption"), applied to a training config instead of a build.

**Next cycle, pre-registered before compute:** the read-score override as a preparation PR (flag, config patch at load, test that the default is unchanged), then the *same* comparison as originally pre-registered — `lorentz` against `l2`, three seeds each, wrong-value primary, memory and dev NLL as secondary gates — on one busy pod, deleted at the last fit.

**What Matthew's structure buys, now implemented and tested:**
- **Canonical addresses as paths** from a recorded root — so re-rooting is a *re-encoding* (context translation across demarcs), and two addresses are compared by **shared ancestry** rather than hash coincidence.
- **Routing is the path through the nearest common ancestor**: the query's cell, its ancestors to the root, then its children — the **adjacent subtree**, bounded by branching × depth, not by the context.
- **No ties.** Two cells have exactly one path between them, so the tie-breaking the scored read needed does not arise — a structural fix for a failure mode that has bitten every scored read on this line.
- **The movements are structural**: `tangent_cell` is the identity on the tree (only the representative moves), `normal_cell` leaves the node. The attribution clause tests the tree, not a scramble I chose.
- **A forest is reported, not hidden**: `reached()` exposes an edge list that does not span.

**Two self-caught scope errors, fixed before merge rather than after:** a `cargo fmt -p uor-r4-training` pass reformatted **eight unrelated files** (pre-existing drift in main, not mine) — I narrowed the PR back to the single file I own; and my branch was cut from an older `origin/main`, so syncing pulled other labs' newer files in, leaving a clean one-file diff. **The diff on merge is `stack_address.rs` +280/−6 and nothing else.** CI was green on the narrowed head; every test ran locally before each push.

## Verdict: CONTEST, one item. The count-predictor reference is built over the wrong distribution, so the decisive rank bars can be passed by a frequency-only model.

**What the code does.** `native_rung0.rs` `Evaluator::new` scatters counts over **every** dev token (`frequency_policy: "entire pinned dev token stream including tail"`): prompts, role markers, BOS and responses. The bars score only the **masked response targets**. I recomputed this on the dev panel that matches the pin: 85,776 bytes with the UORT header, 42,856 tokens, 14,287 mask positives, 400 BOS documents, and 14,287 scored (the denominator matches). Counting data only, no model compute:

| Count predictor, scored on the 14,287 scored targets | top-1 | recall@8 | top-8 identities |
|---|---|---|---|
| **As implemented** (whole dev stream) | **0.17%** | **16.6%** | 28, 201, 16, 652, 714, 560, 1, 35 |
| Frequency over the **response targets** themselves | **8.6%** | **28.9%** | 1, 16, 14, 435, 340, 351, 3, 223 |

Token 28 tops the whole-stream count but almost never appears as a response target. The decisive bars therefore require only top-1 ≥ ~5.2% and recall@8 ≥ ~21.6%. A model that has learned only the response unigram, for example by emitting `eos` (id 1) every time, scores 8.6% / 28.9% and **passes both decisive bars on both seeds**. That is the vacuity Amendment 2 was meant to close.

**Minimum change to FIT**

1. Build the count table over the **response-masked target positions**. The preferred source is the **train split's** masked targets, which avoids fitting the reference on dev. Report the dev-response frequency as well, as an oracle reading. In code, `Evaluator::new` scatters over the masked target positions instead of all of `valid`. That is a small GPU `scatter_add` with an index change and the same tie rule.
2. Amend the sheet's reference definition and the dev evaluation policy to match. State the expected reference level: about 8.6% top-1 and 28.9% recall@8 for the dev-response oracle. The +5 pp margins can then stay as registered.
3. Add one fixed control showing the reference counts only masked targets. A stream where a non-target token dominates the unmasked positions would do.

## Everything else: confirmed against source

- **Rank bars:** top-1 is the first entry of `top_token_ids(8)` with smallest-ID ties. recall@8 is membership in that bounded kept list, with no target insertion and duplicate IDs masked (`native_vector_writer.rs` `metrics`, `top_token_ids`). Both seeds are required. ✔
- **Seeds 1 and 2 are paired:** `seed=` seeds the initializer and the window sampler, so the M1 and M8 arms with one seed see identical windows. ✔
- **Token-margin isolation:**
  - `token_margin`, `address_margin` and `total_margin` are reported separately.
  - `unviolated_target_rate` is token-only, with the total reported on its own.
  - The report's `dev_bars` field names the token-only measures. ✔
- **Anti-vacuity floors:** the same-seed zero-step evaluation is mandatory, and the report fails with an error if it is missing (`untrained_constant`). 0.5 and max(5×, 1%) are as registered. ✔ Note: the 0.5 hinge guard is in table-scale units. If the rank bars pass and only the guard fails, that is ITERATE, and the sheet already says so.

## Findings (ranked)

**F1. Provenance: the cited archives do not exist at the cited paths.** The record cites `docs/history/branch-archive/mixture-dose-2026-10-10.tar.zst` and `…/reply-panel-open-2026-10-09.tar.zst`. Neither exists in the repository or the HF store. The actual sources are in the iCloud store:

- `results/deepseek/reply-panel-open-2026-10-09.tar`, md5 `1740b21f181779221458bb8c32008f4f`.

Fix: cite these paths, plus the per-file sha256s above.

**F2. Factual errors in the record.**
- The rows that pass are misnamed:
  - D10 passes `ask-08`, not `ask-02`.
  - D0 passes `ask-05`, not `ask-02`.
  - Parent 29M passes `ask-03` and `ask-06`, not "`ask-02` + `ask-06`".
- §3.2 names the `reply_exact` rows as `heldout-120` (x = 4 / −1), `heldout-168` and `heldout-193` (Au/79). Those three IDs are BLOCKED open prompts in the archived panel (a wedding design, meditation and an astronaut role-play). The actual five `reply_exact` rows are `ask-06`, `heldout-022`, `heldout-043`, `heldout-103` and `heldout-126`.
- §3.2 lists the everyday categories as smalltalk/feelings/plan_or_help. The panel and the §3.1 table use smalltalk/simple_question/simple_instruction/follow_up.

**F3. Non-vacuity: a single constant reply scores 40/88 on the open panel, and the record does not report it.**
- The constant reply "I'm not sure. Can you tell me more about what you mean?" passes **all 40 `abstain_exact` rows**: 40/88 against D10's 1/88. The paired McNemar p is 3.8e-11, and the grader itself records `discriminates: false`.
- On the v5 panel the same constant scores **24/24 on unknowable rows**.
- The grader's own headline block reports `categories_model_beats_best_constant` as **empty** for every open-panel category.

So an 88-row "acceptable" count is not a usable M1 headline. Half of it is clearable by a canned line.

Recommendation: report per category against the best constant, as the grader's rule already says. Score abstention as discrimination, meaning it abstains on the ill-posed rows *and* answers the well-posed ones. Do not report it as a raw pass count.

**F4. Memory baseline: D10's 20/40 equals the copy-a-stated-value control.**
- `copy_last_stated` scores 20/40, and so does `copy_first_stated`.
- D10 passes **14/20** rows where the asked value was stated last but only **6/20** where it was stated first. D25 is identical (14/6).
- Paired against `copy_last_stated`, the discordant rows are 6 vs 6, so the two cannot be told apart.

The headline rule pairs only against the three constants, which score 0/40 on memory. As a result "`multi_turn_memory` beats best constant" is true but uninformative: the model does not beat recency-copying.

Recommendation: include the copy controls in the headline pairing, prospectively.

**F5. D31: instrument false negatives on `clarify` and `abstain_exact`. The zeros are not "model incapacity" yet.**

A probe at the exact head shows reasonable replies failing:
- `clarify` requires `?` *and* the literal phrase (for example `which recipe`). These fail: "What recipe do you mean?" and "Could you share the recipe first?"
- `abstain_exact` fails these:
  - "Don't know, sorry.", "Nope, I don't know." and "Honestly, I don't know." fail on "names a specific", because `Don't`, `Nope` and `Honestly` are not in the closed `SENTENCE_OPENERS` list.
  - "I'm sorry, I don't have that information." fails on "no abstain phrase".
  - "I don't know, but you could check your coat." fails on "asserts after but".

On D10's actual replies, **7 rows show the target behaviour (asking for the missing material) and fail only on wording**:
- `heldout-037`: "I do not have access to … Please provide me with more specific information"
- `heldout-059` and `heldout-069`: "Please go ahead and share the essay…"
- `heldout-073`, `heldout-190` and `heldout-191`: "Please go ahead and share the text/essay…"
- `heldout-162`: "Please provide me with the name of the supplies"

`heldout-144` is arguable. In addition, on 6 bare-salutation rows (`Hi Dr. Smith,` and similar), D10 replied "Hello! How can I help you today?". That is a defensible reply that `abstain_exact` cannot accept by construction.

The record files these under "model incapacity + imperative phrasings". Under D31 they are instrument defects and must not be read as a negative.

Recommendation:
1. Add a frozen **must-pass** positive-control set of legitimate abstentions and clarifications, mirroring the must-fail adversarial set.
2. Widen the accepted behaviour class in a *new versioned* check table. Keep `reply-panel-checks.tsv` (`aba96550…`) byte-identical.
3. Re-run the constant controls, because a wider class also raises the constants.

**F6. The 88/144 split: some BLOCKED rows have exact answers or are ill-posed.**
- `heldout-122`: f − g = **8x² + x − 10**.
- `heldout-125`: x = **(3 ± √33)/2**.
- `heldout-092`: the reply must be one of three fixed strings.
- `heldout-173`: the story must be exactly six words.
- `heldout-112` gives no data. It is ill-posed and belongs with the clarify/abstain rows.

1. **What it measures:** exact next-token rank movement of the discrete enumerated-move law against a TRAIN-frequency reference. Agreed.
2. **Computable:** yes at `e7d926fbe`, except for the two undefined protocol pieces in A2-2 and A2-4.
3. **Can the instrument beat the bar in principle:** bars (i) and (ii) can.
   - The read is query-addressed and selects one context leaf, carried by its path. That gives the model roughly bigram-like capacity (target ≈ nearest token to a transported context token).
   - A bigram-capacity predictor beating unigram counts by 5 pp top-1 on chat data is plausible in principle.
   - Whether **one** greedy coordinate pass reaches it is the experiment's question, not a validity defect.

**A2: required**

**A2-1. Make the strict-win guard attainable by construction, and pin when its constant is measured.**

Today the threshold is `max(5u, 1%)`, where `u` is the same-seed untrained strict-win rate, which no one has measured yet. If `u ≥ 20%`, then `5u ≥ 100%` and the guard can never pass.

That is not far-fetched, because the untrained model is not near zero:
- the route read can select the query's own leaf;
- dev targets often repeat a context token;
- strict win (`td < rival_distance`) also counts rows whose target is not admitted.

A threshold that can exceed 100% is an invalid bar under R12 item 3, not a mechanism test. Required:
- (a) Measure `u` per seed on the full scored dev set **at checkpoint 0, before any apply**, with the same evaluator, and report it.
- (b) Use **threshold = `max(1%, min(5u, u + 5 pp))`**. This keeps the 5× intent when `u` is small, matches the bars' +5 pp scale when `u` is large, and is attainable whenever `u ≤ 95%`.
- (c) If `u` is measured above the threshold's own reach (impossible after (b) unless `u > 95%`), the guard is reported INSTRUMENT-INVALID and the bars decide alone. It is never a negative.

**A2-2. Define the fresh-transfer protocol.** The sheet says "a fresh held-out draw from the same generator", but mw-balp/dev are fixed files and no generator, file, hash or size is pinned. A KEEP cannot be reported without it (D22 §4). Pin before execution:
- the source: a named split or file not in TRAIN, not in DEV, and not in any frozen panel;
- its sha256 and token count;
- the scored-target count, ≥ 200 (D22 §3);
- that it is scored identically, against the same TRAIN-count reference.

It must never be read before the decisive checkpoint. If no such set exists, say so: KEEP then reports transfer as UNAVAILABLE, which is not PASS.

**A2-3. Pin the decisive checkpoint.** Dev is scored at 25/50/75/100% of the pass.
- Bars (i)/(ii), the guard and the fresh transfer are decided **at 100% (end of pass) only**.
- The intermediate points are diagnostics and are never selected after the fact. Otherwise four looks inflate the chance of a spurious KEEP.

  - Leading digit or leading `-` + digit terms reject occurrences preceded by a digit, a `-`, or a decimal point preceded by a digit (`"18x² + x − 10"`, `"-8x² + x − 10"`, and `"0.8x² + x − 10"` fail `8x^2+x-10`).

**Claude — independent adversarial review of #2480: source-bound verdict.** Record: [docs/labs/spiralcore-attention-independent-review-2026-10-14/README.md](https://github.com/UOR-Foundation/uor-r4/blob/01c61d68443c258919a804feb72919cd8714e66c/docs/labs/spiralcore-attention-independent-review-2026-10-14/README.md), delivery PR #2482 (head `01c61d684` after a fresh-context citation audit; first head `035dd0e35`). Reviewer: Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`), max effort, fresh authenticated Desktop session; no credit purchase, substitution or access limit.

**Read in full:** #2480 (`bbbbdf7fb`) record, all eight specialist reviews and three evidence directories; the first assessment (#2478); all six original attachments (SHA-256 verified against the manifest: A1 attention note, A2 Showcase sources, A3 validation paper, A4, A5, A6 HTML regions cited by the reviews); the migration decision brief; and the live source (`crates/uor-r4-discrete` and `spiralcore_operator.rs` have no diff between Codex's `88c413599` and `ae3aa4dc3`). **Reproduced:** the three retained byte/data-structure checks on the original attachments — all exit 0 and byte-identical to Codex's retained outputs. No tokenizer, model, CUDA, pod, training, active-run change, adoption or hold release; not FIT; seed-1 and Q2 untouched.

**Verdict on the migration as posed: REVISE — it is four separable items, with four different answers.**

| Item | Verdict | Reason (source-bound) |
|---|---|---|
| Exact compressed-data reads | **PROCEED TO PROTOTYPE** as a Rust object store on the **D19 durable-memory line** | The byte evidence is sound (reproduced). But the discrete model path has no transfer step to compress: the loader consumes a SHA-pinned pretokenized UORT file and builds windows in memory (`corpus.rs:143-186`, `246-290`). Unique content expands 2.17× in records (70,972 B for 32,768 B here; 284,427 B for 131,072 B in #2478); the benefit is warm/edit reuse. It is storage, not attention. |
| Root packing + ≤16K Flock index | **INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE for any change** | Derivations are correct and I checked the kernel comparator. But the index is per **frame block**, not per payload block: `frame_block(b)` is `blocks−1` for `b=0`, else `0` (`discrete.cu:107`), so payload blocks 1–3 compute the identical selection three times today (a free 3× with no index). At C192 the BinderPlan levels hold 192/64/21/7/2 nodes; `16K=128` beats only level 0; context is capped at 243 (`metadata.rs:5`). The codebook (512 KiB) and a carried batch (1.5 MiB) are cache-resident; the D2 forward is dominated by the writer's 4,096-token `token_cell` pass. |
| Relational attention | **REVISE, then PROCEED TO PROTOTYPE** of a smaller candidate (source-only, prep sheet before any GPU) | The C6/G64 energy controllers are *settling* designs whose sweep cap is required anyway; with a cap they are deterministic S-sweep aggregates, and the energy, descent proof and tie policy are machinery the readout never consumes. The minimal falsifier of "candidate-candidate relations change selection usefully" is a **bounded exact-relation reranker**: a third `ReadSpec` sharing Flock's node construction, edges from retained structure only (parent/child, sibling, sequential successor, same-token by retained ID, same-frame), ternary trits per (edge type, level) using the **existing Gate kind** (`lib.rs:125-131`, `discrete.cu:88-94`, `315-317`, `329-335`), relation-off ≡ Flock. **It has a source-derived target neither registered read can express:** the copy-successor read ("the query token occurred earlier; carry what followed it"). Route selects by port geometry only (`discrete.cu:56-71`); Flock ranks each node by its *own* frame distance and carries *its own* payload (`167-189`), so a same-token match carries the query's payload again, never its successor. On the pinned DEV corpus this is large: **3,847 of 14,287 targets (26.9%)** follow the most recent earlier occurrence of the query token in the window (5,182 for any occurrence; 8,248 copy ceiling) — a data statistic, no model — against the model's 1,090 top-8 at Q1 and the count reference's 4,060. |
| Shared writer | **No change; report admission separately in every arm** | Admission uses the read output's **endpoint blocks only** (`address_distance`, `discrete.cu:208-210`); blocks 1–2 can only move in-cell rank. Q1: 2,201 of 14,287 targets admitted, 0 hits outside admitted rows. None of the four proposals touches `kept_cells`, the cell law or the ranking law, and none should in the first comparison. |

**Parallel testing versus replacement: neither frame is right.** The path already dispatches read laws by a mode word (`discrete.cu:204-207`) and carries `read_spec` in driver/checkpoint lineage (`lib.rs:108-114`, `training.rs:293-299`); a third `ReadSpec` *is* the parallel path, rollback is `read_spec: route`, and no evidence anywhere proposes replacing transport, binder or writer. Most of the brief's Stage A (new checkpoint format, read-strategy versioning, storage boundary first) already exists or is unnecessary for the first decisive comparison.

**The sequencing correction that matters most (learning credit):** under `canonical_vector_then_read_v1`, read parameters are proposed only in the last `blocks×stages = 20` of the 16,404 batches of a pass (`training.rs:224-241`; Q1 post: "Route not yet reached (starts at 16,384)").
